minutes.headline: Cemetery board approved Fish Street monument repairs and higher lighting costs; will review raising burial lot rates.
minutes.summary: The Cemetery Commission reviewed its budget and expenditures, approved a monument company's contract to repair and reset headstones and install a new bronze plaque at Fish Street cemetery, and approved a higher-than-expected cost for the solar lighting project after switching electricians. Members discussed raising burial-lot and perpetual-care rates before the new North Cemetery expansion opens, continued researching cemetery grants, and set a work session and next regular meeting date.

votes.motion: Approve the November 14 minutes regarding the Fish Street site visit
Approve the work by Runster Monument Company for the Fish Street monuments and plaque
Approve the increased cost for the different electrician on the solar lighting project
Adjourn the meeting (captioned as "add another meeting today at 7:25 p.m.")

budget_items.what_was_said: An amount voted at the recent special town meeting was added into the site-improvements capital article, bringing the balance available to spend.
The sale-of-lots fund balance was reduced by the amount moved into the capital article, leaving a new balance.
Interest available to spend from perpetual care was stated, along with how much had been spent, leaving a remaining balance.
A trust fund expenditure for a cabinet was noted as already paid.
The original town-meeting-approved budget for the back lot expansion was noted, with a small amount spent so far on the original survey.

budget_items.topic: Burial rights / sale of lots revenue, FY26
budget_items.what_was_said: Revenue from three lots sold so far this fiscal year was discussed, split between burial rights and perpetual care per lot sold.
Prior fiscal year totals for perpetual care and burial rights revenue were read off a sheet, along with a separate cremation-lot figure.
The superintendent corrected an earlier estimate given for the bronze plaque, plus a separate charge for extra work already done; the minutes were left as written with this correction noted verbally.
The wall project's cost was corrected from an earlier figure to a slightly higher one.

budget_items.topic: Fish Street monument/plaque contract (Runster Monument Company)
budget_items.what_was_said: A quote for washing, pinning, and installing headstones and a bronze plaque, including repair of damaged stones, was reviewed and approved; remaining capital funds would be split between this work and other south cemetery work.

Costs for the solar lights, a lift rental, and an electrician were itemized; because a different (busier) electrician was used, the total came in higher than what commissioners had previously approved.
The lift rental invoice amount was adjusted downward to remove a municipal tax exemption amount before being submitted for payment.

transfers.description: $10,000 approved at special town meeting added into the site-improvements capital article, taken out of the sale-of-lots fund balance line
transfers.outcome: voted (at prior town meeting; noted here as booked)

transfers.description: Remaining capital funds discussed as needing to be moved from planned south cemetery work toward finishing the Fish Street project before town meeting

decisions.decision: The November 19 minutes were left approved as written, with a verbal correction noted that the plaque cost was $1,200 rather than $2,000, plus $800 for extra work.
The board agreed to compare Lunenburg's burial-rights and perpetual-care rates to other towns before opening the new large lot section, rather than raising rates immediately.
Ordering of the Fish Street bronze plaque was deferred until the wording/layout for the Goodrich family plaque is finalized, but the monument company was authorized to proceed with the stone work.
Reimbursement forms for the lighting-project vendors would be filled out and signed immediately after the work is done, rather than waiting for the normal warrant cycle, to speed up payment.
A work session at the North Cemetery was set for Friday, December 19, at 8:00 a.m. to review the cemetery's rules and regulations.
The next regular Cemetery Commission meeting was set for January 22.
The superintendent's compiled letters/thank-yous were agreed to be made part of the public record and posted publicly.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to approve Runster Monument Company's contract to repair and reset Fish Street headstones and install a bronze plaque, though ordering the plaque itself was held until wording is finalized.
The commission voted to approve a higher cost than previously budgeted for the solar lighting project after the work went to a different, busier electrician.
Rather than raise burial-lot and perpetual-care rates now, members agreed to compare Lunenburg's rates to other towns before the new North Cemetery expansion opens for sale.
A work session at North Cemetery to review its rules and regulations was set for December 19, with the next regular meeting set for January 22.

why_it_matters: Burial-lot and perpetual-care rates, which affect anyone planning to buy a plot at the new North Cemetery expansion, are under review before that section opens.
Capital funds set aside for cemetery site improvements are being spent on Fish Street monument repair and solar lighting, and the lighting cost came in above what was previously approved.
The plaque commemorating the Goodrich family plot at Fish Street is on hold until its wording is finalized, so that specific piece of the approved contract has not yet moved forward.
